# The in-game dump hashes, two lines per engine.
#
#   <engine> <row> <data-sha256> <settings-sha256> <mod set, name@version, sorted>
#
# ENGINE, because a dump is a function of the engine that produced it: a new
# Factorio moves base prototypes and every hash with them, and a line keyed by
# version lets one file hold several without either one being wrong.
#
# THE ROW, default or flipped, because the dump is also a function of the
# settings the engine read. The default row is every setting where the mod
# declared it, which is the load a player who never opens the settings screen
# gets. The flipped row is testdata/ingame/flipped.json written into the mod
# directory as mod-settings.dat by `fklua modsettings write`: a player-typed
# ingredient list that takes a dropdown's chosen preset over and carries a fluid
# and a fractional amount, a research cost overridden whole with a TYPO in its
# pack text, a whole ingredient list typed into a setting with no dropdown in
# front of it, and a TYPO in an ingredient text beside a dropdown that decides.
# Only the engine can walk those paths, because the settings stage stores a
# value and no stand-in has one to read back. The two typos are what say a
# refused player text LOADS, one per channel: the row exits 0, the research
# comes out priced on the packs the chosen TIER carries, the quench recipe comes
# out of the preset its dropdown names, and the log carries exactly two ERROR
# lines. The pack typo alone was a run that exited 1 and wrote no dump to hash
# before the fallback decision; the INGREDIENT typo was one again after it,
# because the note a recipe carries to disclose a fallback is 266 bytes as the
# ELEMENT the engine measures, newline included, against a 200-byte-per-element
# ceiling, and the library chunks every composed literal now.
#
# THE BYTES OF THAT FILE ARE PINNED TOO, beside this one as flipped.golden.dat.
# The writer belongs to the toolchain now, so the gate compares what it
# produces for flipped.json against those bytes on every run and a codec change
# upstream fails on the file rather than only on a hash of a dump. Both goldens
# are re-recorded by the same --update.
#
# THE TWO ROWS SHARE A SETTINGS HASH, and that is correct rather than
# suspicious: setting PROTOTYPES are what mod-settings-dump.json holds, and a
# stored value moves the data dump without moving a prototype.
#
# TWO HASHES, because setting prototypes never reach the data dump: a golden
# over the data dump alone stays green for a guest whose settings stage did
# nothing at all.
#
# THE MOD SET, because the dump is a function of every mod that ran. Factorio's
# bundled DLC data loads whatever --mod-directory says, so a machine owning
# different DLC produces a different dump for a mod that is perfectly fine.
# A mismatch here is ENVIRONMENTAL and reports SKIPPED, not FAILED.
#
# THE 2.1.17 ROWS' SETTINGS HASH IS DERIVED AND NOT CAPTURED (2026-09-22, and
# written by hand a third time that day when the surface half landed). No
# 2.1.17 binary is on this machine, and every round since has moved composed
# setting descriptions, so those two rows would otherwise carry a hash this
# library no longer produces. What is written there is the 2.0.77 capture's
# settings hash, on the golden's own documented property that all four rows
# share one: a setting prototype is this library's own and no engine has moved
# one. A 2.1 machine confirms or refutes the derivation loudly, by running the
# gate: a mismatch there is a failure and not a skip.
#
# AND THEIR DATA HASHES ARE STALE, which is new and is stated rather than
# guessed. The surface half's fixture adds three prototypes to the example
# guest, two recipes and a technology, so the data dump moved on every engine
# and the values below are the ones a 2.1.17 run produced BEFORE it. They are
# left as recorded rather than derived, because nothing here can compute a data
# hash for an engine it cannot run: a 2.1 machine re-records both rows with
# `scripts/run-ingame.sh --update`, and until it does the 2.1 arm of this gate
# fails on those two rows by design. The 2.0.77 rows below are captured and
# current.
#
# AND --update WRITES THE ENGINE IT RAN ON LAST, so the 2.0.77 rows sit under
# the 2.1.17 ones here. The order carries no meaning: the gate looks its own
# engine up by the first field.
#
# Capture both rows with: scripts/run-ingame.sh --update

2.1.17 flipped 83c45b19038a8cc140dfc19b381ffabb94159084ec24812eadb04fbf662451db 501288857a1251460f5924506abd3dfcc40c676835ab57f4fc2fc388fda240a4 base@2.1.17 core@0.0.0 elevated-rails@2.1.17 fkrecipes-example@0.1.0 quality@2.1.17 recycler@2.1.17 space-age@2.1.17
